bounded_leaf: Inspect only exact TaskManager implementation/tests for duplicate, partial, unknown and already-answered tasks/update inputResponses key behavior; derive the smallest restart-safe anti-replay/input-key lifecycle rule compatible with the prior cancellation finding.
observations: TaskContext::request_input inserts each key into used_input_keys before inserting it into pending_inputs; reusing any key during the in-memory task lifetime is an error.

TaskManager::update_task sweeps expiry, requires a known task id, then independently removes each supplied key from pending_inputs. Only a removed pending key is delivered to its oneshot sender; absent keys are ignored. Therefore partial response sets are accepted, and duplicate/already-answered/unknown-or-superseded keys on a known task are no-ops.

An unknown task id is an INVALID_PARAMS error; the exact unit test unknown_task_is_invalid_params covers get/cancel/update. The exact input_required_roundtrip test covers one pending key becoming answered and the task completing.

The exact test suite in this file does not contain dedicated duplicate-key, partial-update, or already-answered update tests; those three semantics are pinned by the update_task implementation and its source contract, not by dedicated tests. This scope distinction is preserved.

Because stock pending_inputs contains process-local oneshot senders and used_input_keys is process memory, neither answered-key tombstones nor pending response delivery survive a server restart in stock TaskManager.

derived_minimal_durable_rule.rule: Persist a per-task, never-reused input-key record with monotonic states PENDING -> ANSWERED -> APPLIED, plus PENDING -> INVALIDATED for cancellation/supersession. A key record is a lifetime tombstone: request_input must reject every previously created key regardless of terminal substate. tasks/update may atomically change only PENDING to ANSWERED and retain the response payload durably; updates for ANSWERED, APPLIED, INVALIDATED or absent keys on a known task are no-ops. Partial maps apply each key independently. Cancellation must durably change still-PENDING keys to INVALIDATED before acknowledging cancel. Restart may redeliver a durable ANSWERED payload only to the authoritative task attempt/generation; it must never reopen ANSWERED/APPLIED/INVALIDATED as PENDING. APPLIED is recorded only with or after durable operation progress that proves the response no longer needs redelivery.
derived_minimal_durable_rule.why_answered_retains_payload: A single PENDING->consumed tombstone without the response value loses an accepted response if the process crashes after accepting tasks/update but before the operation durably consumes it. Keeping ANSWERED(response) separates protocol acceptance from operation application and permits restart redelivery without accepting the same client response twice.
derived_minimal_durable_rule.cancellation_ordering_scope: This preserves the prior exact finding for still-pending inputs: cancel invalidates them before ack so late old responses cannot regain authority. If an update wins the atomic transition first, the key is already ANSWERED and is historical accepted input; later cancellation remains cooperative and must be resolved by the task attempt/generation fence rather than by reopening the key.
not_proven: Stock rmcp does not implement this persistent state machine or restart redelivery.
This rule alone does not provide persistent task creation, restart execution liveness, or exactly-once external effects.
No compile/runtime experiment was executed in this slice.
